newsitem.title: USA: OMB's Raines says no progress yet for budget pact.
newsitem.headline: OMB's Raines says no progress yet for budget pact.

text.p: White House budget director Franklin Raines said Tuesday no measureable progress had been made with Congressional Republicans on reaching a budget accord.

"The only thing going on, as has been going on for the last several weeks, I talk to as many people as I can to see if we can make some progress. But as of now, we're not making any measureable progress...towards getting agreement," Raines told Reuters after testifying at a House Appropriations subcommittee hearing.
Raines called "very unhelpful" a resolution expected to be considered by the House of Representatives seeking that President Clinton submit another budget plan.
There was no chance the White House would re-submit its budget, Raines, director of the Office of Management and Budget, said.
"We will not do it. The resolution is unhelpful, it will not lead to any progress, what we need to do is balance the budget," Raines said.
Republicans say Clinton's budget does not reach balance in 2002, while the White House says the president's budget does reach balance.
